The Argand diagram above shows the roots of a quartic polynomial $f(x).$ Determine the **expanded form** of $f(x)$ given that the coefficient of the quartic term is $3.$

$f(x)=$
{{field-1}}
$-\,81$
worked_solution:
From the diagram, we see that $f(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1}=-3,$ ${x}_{1}=1,$ and ${x}_{3,4}=\pm 3\text{i}.$ Additionally, we're given that the coefficient of the quartic term is $a=3.$ Therefore, we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3})(x-{x}_{4}) \\  & =3(x-(-3))(x-1)(x-(-3\text{i}))(x-3\text{i}) \\  & =3(x+3)(x-1)(x+3\text{i})(x-3\text{i})\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}3(x+3)(x-1)(x+3\text{i})(x-3\text{i}) & = \\ 3({x}^{2}-x+3x-3)({x}^{2}-3\text{i}x+3\text{i}x-(3\text{i})^{2}) & = \\ 3({x}^{2}+2x-3)({x}^{2}+9) & = \\ 3({x}^{4}+9{x}^{2}+2{x}^{3}+18x-3{x}^{2}-27) & = \\ 3({x}^{4}+2{x}^{3}+6{x}^{2}+18x-27) & = \\ 3{x}^{4}+6{x}^{3}+18{x}^{2}+54x-81 & .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $f(x)=3{x}^{4}+6{x}^{3}+18{x}^{2}+54x\,-81.$
